passages.original: dic nobis, Hebræus autem dixit : Quia protomartyr Stephanus est, et in ipso vita mea et spes mea 2, quia viderunt oculi mei gloriosissima hodie. Tunc venien- tes protectores nuntiaverunt Imperatori, quia proto- martyr Stephanus est. Et gavisus est valde, et convo- cans Eusebium episcopum dicit ei : Vade ad navim cum multitudine populi, et ego mittam plaustrum, et ferte mihi loculum in palatium.
passages.english: Tell us." And the Hebrew said: "It is the protomartyr Stephen, and in him is my life and my hope, because my eyes have seen most glorious things today." Then the guards came and reported to the Emperor that it was the protomartyr Stephen. And he rejoiced greatly, and calling Bishop Eusebius he said to him: "Go to the ship with a multitude of the people, and I will send a wagon, and bring the coffin to me in the palace."
passages.notes: The passage opens mid-speech: "Tell us" completes the guards' question begun in the preceding context ("What spectacle is it?"). The "2" after "spes mea" is a footnote mark from the printed edition and has been omitted. "Protectores" is rendered "guards"; the term denotes members of the imperial bodyguard.
